# Temporary Voice Rooms Checklist: Temporary Voice Room Creation

**Purpose**: Review the temporary-room requirements for clarity, completeness, consistency, and measurable acceptance before implementation.
**Created**: 2026-08-31
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are trigger-channel and destination-category requirements specified for every configured Discord server? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK002 Are requirements defined for eligible members, bots, unrelated channel transitions, and unconfigured servers without relying on unstated defaults? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, §FR-009, §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK003 Are room creation, association, stale-room replacement, and room reuse requirements all documented as distinct outcomes? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003, §FR-005, §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK004 Are requirements defined for retaining an association after movement failure and retrying that existing room later? [Completeness, Spec §FR-011]

## Requirement Clarity and Consistency

- [ ] CHK005 Is the canonical meaning of “active temporary room” clear across the one-room rule, stale-room handling, and movement-failure retry behavior? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005–§FR-007, §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK006 Is “entry to the configured trigger channel” unambiguous enough to distinguish a qualifying transition from duplicate delivery and unrelated voice-state updates? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK007 Is the room-name requirement sufficiently specific about predictability, user-friendliness, and derived-member input without conflicting with privacy requirements? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK008 Are the requirements consistent in treating unconfigured-server events as ignored while treating invalid configuration for configured servers as observable failures? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014, §FR-016, Edge Cases]

## Concurrency and Recovery Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK009 Are requirements explicit that the one-active-room limit applies separately to every member within each Discord server? [Coverage, Spec §FR-007, Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK010 Are requirements explicit that same-member duplicate or concurrent trigger events cannot create more than one active room at any point? [Coverage, Spec §FR-007, User Story 3]
- [ ] CHK011 Are independent-concurrency requirements defined for different members, including the expected absence of cross-member blocking? [Coverage, Spec §FR-008, §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK012 Are recovery requirements complete for a deleted associated room, room-creation failure, member-movement failure, and a later valid event? [Coverage, Spec §FR-006, §FR-010, §FR-011, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK013 Are requirements clear about the intended result when a member leaves or changes channels while room creation is in progress? [Edge Case, Spec Edge Cases]

## Configuration, Privacy, and Observability Requirements

- [ ] CHK014 Is the per-server configuration mapping requirement clear about identifier validity, server scoping, and the treatment of absent entries? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001, §FR-014, §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK015 Are configuration-error requirements explicit enough to distinguish missing or invalid configured values from an intentionally unconfigured server? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014, §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK016 Are requirements explicit about which operational failures must be observable and which sensitive data must be excluded from that evidence? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010, §FR-011, §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK017 Is “unnecessary personal identifiers” defined or bounded sufficiently to permit consistent review of privacy-safe observations? [Ambiguity, Spec User Story 3, §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK018 Are readiness and lifecycle preservation requirements consistent with every create, move, configuration, and Discord-operation failure scenario? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010–§FR-012]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK019 Can the five-second successful assignment target be measured consistently for both newly created and reused rooms? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK020 Do the concurrency success criteria specify representative duplicate and multi-member conditions that cover the one-room and independence requirements? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-002, §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK021 Does the failure success criterion define sufficiently objective evidence that the worker accepts a later valid event without exposing sensitive data? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK022 Are documentation success criteria clear about the per-server configuration information a developer must be able to supply? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §FR-014, §SC-005]

## Scope and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK023 Are excluded cleanup, persistence, permissions, limits, rename, and command capabilities clearly separated from the retained-association retry requirement? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011, §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK024 Are assumptions about transient process state, Discord permissions, and simulated Discord support documented as dependencies that reviewers can validate? [Dependencies, Spec Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
- Add comments or findings inline.
- Link to relevant resources or documentation.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference.
